clips.text_zh: 又睇到Doge post。3日內爆space，叫我哋ap。贏就贏，輸就當SNL 2.0學費囉lol。唔買又驚miss，買咗又驚接刀，真係廢柴。🙏
clips.text_en_b1: Doge goes to fucking space in three days and you are not buying. If this shit explodes it will still move up, so why not ape a bit, then sell so it does not become SNL 2.0. Or maybe it will just start the hype again. The setup is right there if you are not too scared.

signal.rationale: OP frames a 3-day catalyst event with defined risk plan to sell before it can become SNL 2.0

clips.text_en_b2: Doge is about to shoot into fucking space within three days, and you're still sitting on the fence. If it actually explodes, even a modest position will ride the wave, so throwing in a small ape makes sense provided you take profits before it collapses into another SNL-style pump and dump. The setup is staring you in the face, but fear is holding you back. Buy the dip if it comes.
clips.text_en_c1: Doge appears poised for a parabolic move within roughly seventy-two hours, with multiple signals suggesting an imminent breakout. The dilemma is fundamentally psychological: positioning oneself in advance carries the risk of catching a falling knife, while abstaining almost guarantees regret should momentum accelerate. The pragmatic compromise, which I am inclined toward, involves allocating a modest tranche and exiting before any euphoria peaks, lest this cycle repeat the SNL-induced collapse that wiped out late entrants. Were the setup to falter, the loss would amount to nothing more than tuition paid for another lesson in speculative excess. The pattern, however, remains textbook: consolidation at the lows, sentiment rebuilding, liquidity quietly accumulating.
clips.text_en_c2: The Doge chatter is, once again, impossible to ignore. Apparently we are looking at a celestial ascent within the next seventy-two hours, which is, of course, the cue for the board to commence aping into positions with the usual fervour. The calculus is rather straightforward: if the move materialises, there is still ample upside to ride, and if it does not, one simply treats the loss as a tuition fee for having been snubbed by the SNL fiasco all over again. Yet the deeper affliction lies in the perennial paralysis of conviction, since abstaining invites the dread of having missed the trade, while participating summons the ever-present spectre of catching a falling knife.

clips.text_zh: 10年揀一樣hold，Bitcoin定黃金？問咗全世界都係呢句。我揀BTC，黃金太慢，但黃金仔都識郁lol。命理都話今年金水弱，可能啦。
clips.text_en_b1: Bitcoin versus gold. If you had to hold only one for the next ten years, would you choose Bitcoin or gold. What makes your choice better than the other. Think about store of value, supply growth, and how each behaves in a real crisis. Ten years is a long time.

signal.rationale: OP asks a framing question; implied bias is to overweight BTC over gold for a 10-year horizon

clips.text_en_b2: The classic dilemma: if you had to hold a single asset for the next ten years, would you pick Bitcoin or gold? I lean towards BTC because gold simply moves too slowly, although even bullion manages to creep up these days. Proponents of the metal point to weak metal-water energy this year in Chinese metaphysics, so the timing might favour gold. Either way, store of value matters.
clips.text_en_c1: Forced into a ten-year time horizon with a single asset, the choice between Bitcoin and gold reduces to a question of monetary velocity and demographic demand. Gold, whose supply grows at roughly one to two percent annually, has functioned as a crisis hedge for millennia; it moves, albeit glacially, particularly when traditional metal indices flicker with seasonal conviction. Bitcoin, by contrast, offers a fixed issuance schedule, programmatic scarcity, and an addressable audience increasingly comfortable with self-custody. The deciding factor for me is portability: an entire position can traverse borders in a seed phrase, whereas bullion invites confiscation risk.
clips.text_en_c2: The perennial question resurfaces with monotonous inevitability: were one compelled to hold a single asset for the ensuing decade, would one elect Bitcoin or gold, and on what rigorously articulated premise? The unvarnished reality is that gold, whatever its venerated status as a store of value, exhibits a glacial rate of appreciation that borders on the somnolent, whereas Bitcoin, for all its contortions, remains structurally positioned to outperform during any sustained period of monetary debasement. Supply trajectories, crisis-era correlations, and the relative velocity of capital appreciation must all be weighed against the inertia of bullion. Even the more pedestrian gold equities, it must be conceded, possess a modest capacity for movement, though scarcely enough to vindicate the proposition.

clips.text_zh: 今日再做slope survey。factor of safety數晒出嚟，但contractor問點解用soil nailing唔用其他。我答唔晒，英文又窒。Tommy叫我下星期interview要有理據。🧐
clips.text_en_b1: Slope survey today. Factor of safety is calculated for every section, but the contractor asked why we used soil nailing instead of other methods. I could not explain all the reasons, and my English broke down. My boss told me I need clear reasoning for the interview next week.
clips.source_hint: /biz/ generic macro post, repurposed as site-work language
clips.text_en_b2: I was out on a slope survey today, crunching the factor of safety for every section, when the contractor fired off a tricky question: why soil nailing rather than any of the alternative methods? I struggled to articulate the reasoning, and my English kept falling apart halfway through my explanations. My boss, Tommy, has made it clear that the interview next week demands solid technical justification, not vague hand-waving.
clips.text_en_c1: I spent the morning conducting a slope stability survey, working through the factor-of-safety calculations for each delineated section. The numerical results, fortunately, were coherent across the board; it was the subsequent technical dialogue that exposed my limitations. The contractor, reasonably enough, pressed me on why soil nailing had been specified over alternative reinforcement methods such as rock bolting or retaining structures, and I found myself groping for half-formed justifications while my English, already strained, began to unravel entirely. Tommy later informed me that the upcoming client interview will demand not merely calculations but articulate, defensible reasoning.
clips.text_en_c2: Another day spent conducting slope surveys, and the factor of safety has been dutifully tabulated for each discretised section, yet the moment the contractor pressed me on why soil nailing was specified in lieu of alternative stabilisation measures, I found myself thoroughly outmanoeuvred. The technical justification is by no means obscure, but articulating the comparative advantages of soil nailing over, say, reinforced earth or gravity retaining systems, with the requisite engineering precision, proved altogether beyond my linguistic means. My English, for want of a more charitable descriptor, simply disintegrated under the pressure. Tommy has since intimated, in his characteristically unsentimental fashion, that the forthcoming interview will demand not merely competent answers but a defensible rationale rooted in first principles, which, given my present predicament, suggests that the intervening week will be spent in a state…

clips.text_zh: 夜晚溫FE，load path由beam去column到foundation。concept識，但講唔出點樣check shear connection，英文真係廢。考牌都未完，又燒時間。
clips.text_en_b1: Studying for the FE exam at night. Load path goes from beam to column down to the foundation. I understand the concept, but I cannot explain how to check the shear connection in clear English. The professional license is not done yet and I am burning time again.
clips.source_hint: /biz/ macro post, repurposed for structural English
clips.text_en_b2: Burning the midnight oil on FE exam revision again. The load path concept is fairly straightforward, running from beam down through the column and into the foundation, yet when it comes to explaining how to verify the shear connection in clear English, I completely draw a blank. The professional licence still isn't in the bag, and I'm haemorrhaging time on language rather than actual engineering content.
clips.text_en_c1: Another evening buried in Fundamentals of Engineering revision, tracing the load path conceptually from beam to column and ultimately down to the foundation. The theoretical sequence is intuitive enough; where I falter is in articulating how one systematically verifies the shear connection in a manner that satisfies an examiner's expectations. My spoken English, regrettably, disintegrates the moment precision is required, and the professional licensure process, still incomplete, continues to consume hours I can scarcely spare. Each session reinforces the same uncomfortable conclusion: technical comprehension and professional communication are distinct competencies, and neglecting the latter undermines the former regardless of how solid the underlying calculation may be.
clips.text_en_c2: Evening revision for the Fundamentals of Engineering examination has, once again, devolved into a rather humbling exercise in confronting the chasm between conceptual understanding and articulate expression. The load path in question traverses from the beam through the column down to the foundation, a sequence I can sketch with the confidence of long acquaintance, yet when pressed to elucidate the methodology for verifying the shear connection in lucid, technically defensible prose, my command of the English language betrays a rather conspicuous inadequacy. The professional licensure remains, as ever, a work in progress, and the realisation that time is being expended without commensurate intellectual return is, to put it mildly, galling.

clips.text_zh: Dario、Sam、Elon三個突然一齊叫政府監管AI？opensource model追上就即刻想被regulate，擺明係想鎖死對手lol。AI遲早殺埋藍領同白領，我仲考咩牌。
clips.text_en_b1: Dario Amodei says we need government regulation. Sam Altman says we need government regulation. Elon Musk says we need government regulation. I see what they are doing here. Funny how they start screaming come regulate us right after open-source models are catching up to the frontier.
clips.source_hint: /g/ thread on AI CEOs all calling for regulation at once
clips.text_en_b2: So Dario Amodei, Sam Altman, and Elon Musk all suddenly cry out for sweeping government regulation of AI, in perfect unison. Funny how that chorus only kicked off once open-source models started closing the gap on frontier systems. The playbook is glaringly obvious: rope in regulators to strangle the competition before they catch up. Meanwhile, the technology marches on, devouring both blue-collar and white-collar jobs alike.
clips.text_en_c1: It is hardly coincidental that Dario Amodei, Sam Altman, and Elon Musk have converged, almost in unison, on a single public message: government must regulate artificial intelligence before it spirals beyond oversight. The choreography of these statements, emerging precisely as open-source models begin approaching frontier capability, betrays a strategic calculus that should not escape anyone paying attention. Frontier laboratories, having exhausted their first-mover advantage, now seek regulatory moats that would entrench incumbents while strangling nascent competitors in compliance overhead.
clips.text_en_c2: It is, to put it charitably, a remarkable spectacle: Dario Amodei, Sam Altman, and Elon Musk, those erstwhile champions of unfettered innovation, suddenly discover, in remarkable unison, an urgent and previously latent affection for governmental oversight of artificial intelligence. The timing, one cannot help but observe, is nothing if not propitious, given that open-source models have, in recent months, narrowed the gap with frontier systems to a degree that must occasion considerable unease in certain boardrooms. The stratagem is scarcely veiled: invoke the precautionary principle, entreat the regulators to intervene, and thereby inscribe, in the language of statute, a moat that protects incumbency from competitive disruption.

clips.text_zh: Pol板講全球糧食危機，5億人湧去美墨邊境，最後都係美國食晒。對我嚟講，反而想快啲返Florida，起碼糧食平啲lol。
clips.text_en_b1: You realize this means global famine. Nobody wants to talk about it because there is no solution. It is like a meteor headed straight for earth. Sure mostly Africa and South Asia will starve, but that is only the beginning. It will trigger mass migration into the US on a scale the world has never seen.
clips.source_hint: /pol/ thread warning about coming global famine and migration
clips.text_en_b2: Take a step back and you'll see this spells out global famine on a catastrophic scale. Nobody wants to confront the issue because there genuinely is no clean solution. Sure, Africa and South Asia will bear the initial brunt, yet that crisis will cascade outwards, triggering mass migration towards the US border on a magnitude the world has never witnessed. America's the final destination, and food prices will skyrocket accordingly.
clips.text_en_c1: The geopolitical board has been discussing cascading food insecurity, and the trajectory, though unfashionable to acknowledge, points toward systemic collapse rather than localised disruption. A projected half-billion displaced persons would, by any historical precedent, converge on the most agriculturally productive hemisphere available, namely the United States, whose grain belts would absorb demands they were never designed to meet. The result would be inflationary pressure severe enough to render current grocery prices almost quaint by comparison. Personally, the calculus has become unexpectedly straightforward: returning to Florida sooner rather than later may be prudent, if only because caloric expenditure per dollar remains comparatively tolerable there.
clips.text_en_c2: The discussion on the political board concerning the impending global food crisis has, regrettably, the ring of apocalyptic prophecy, yet the discomfiting truth is that scarcely anyone is prepared to confront the implications with the candour they deserve, principally because no palatable solution presents itself. The trajectory resembles that of an errant celestial body on an inexorable collision course, and while the initial casualties will be absorbed, with characteristic grim predictability, by sub-Saharan Africa and South Asia, one must understand that mass starvation at that scale is never merely a regional affliction. The subsequent displacement will, in all likelihood, manifest as an unprecedented migratory torrent toward the southern border of the United States, a phenomenon for which no historical analogue adequately prepares us, and whose secondary effects, economic and otherwise, will reorder the geopolitical landscape…

clips.text_zh: 睇到個fit帖同我情況好似。2025年83kg肥，cut到65kg廢，之後lean bulk返80kg。bench 1板、squat 90、dead 120。但係flat，我覺得我仲係skinnyfat。肥仔信一定笑我。
clips.text_en_b1: In May 2025 I was 83kg fat with almost no muscle. Aggressive cut until mid-April 2026, I was 65kg skinnyfat and could barely bench the 20kg bar. Then I leaned bulk to now, back up to 80kg. Flat bench 3x8 one plate, squat 3x6 90kg, deadlift 3x8 120kg. I look different but still feel flat.
clips.source_hint: /fit/ classic skinnyfat-to-bulk progress and cut timing question
clips.text_en_b2: Back in May 2025 I tipped the scales at 83kg with barely any muscle to speak of. I went on an aggressive cut that dragged me down to a miserable 65kg by mid-April 2026, pathetically skinnyfat and struggling to bench even the empty bar. Since then I've leaned bulk steadily back up to 80kg, hitting a flat bench of one plate, squatting 90kg, and pulling 120kg on deadlifts. My physique has shifted, but I still look flat, and doubt keeps creeping in.
clips.text_en_c1: My trajectory bears an uncanny resemblance to that of the original poster, and the parallels are instructive if not entirely reassuring. In May 2025, I tipped the scales at eighty-three kilograms with negligible muscle mass; an aggressive cut through mid-April 2026 left me at a gaunt sixty-five, barely capable of pressing the unweighted bar. A subsequent lean bulk has restored me to roughly eighty kilograms, with flat bench now at three plates for sets of eight, squat at ninety kilograms for six, and deadlift at one-twenty for eight.
clips.text_en_c2: The fitness thread in question mirrored my own circumstances with an accuracy that bordered on the uncanny, and so I find myself compelled to recount the rather protracted chronology of my own transformation. In May of 2025, I presented at eighty-three kilograms, adipose tissue predominating, with musculature so negligible as to render the term generous. An aggressive caloric deficit was subsequently imposed, which, by the following April, had reduced me to sixty-five kilograms of what can only be described as the quintessential skinnyfat phenotype, scarcely capable of pressing an unloaded Olympic bar.
